41	## Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts
42	
43	Passing flow data into an inline agent requires **three hand-authored, aligned** pieces. **The CLI does not derive the input wiring** — `uip agent refresh` does **not** scan prompts, derive `inputSchema`, or populate `agentInputVariables`; you author all three, and packaging ships them as-authored. (Refresh *does* regenerate `messages[].contentTokens` from `content` — that's the one derived part; see the invariant below.) The converter builds the runtime `JobArguments` from the **flow node's `inputs.agentInputVariables[]`** (not from `$vars` tokens in `agent.json`). Flatten rule: `$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>` → `<trigger>__output__<var>`.
44	
45	The three pieces — **Delivery** (node `agentInputVariables[]`), **Contract** (`agent.json` `inputSchema`), and **Resolution** (`{{input.<key>}}` in `messages[].content`) — and their examples are in the table below. `flow validate` catches a Resolution↔Contract mismatch (a `{{input.K}}` that's malformed or names a key not in `inputSchema`), but a missing/wrong **Delivery** binding passes validate and only shows up as empty input at `flow debug`. Agent-side `inputSchema`/`contentTokens` mechanics: the `uipath-agents` skill's [inline-in-flow § Wiring Flow Inputs Into an Inline Agent](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md#wiring-flow-inputs-into-an-inline-agent-required).
46	
47	> **Prerequisite — the bound value must actually exist as a variable.** A node binding `=$vars.X` resolves at runtime only if `$vars.X` is a declared variable. `flow validate` does **not** check that the path exists — a binding referencing an undeclared trigger field passes validate, then **faults at debug** with `JobArguments` empty. When the upstream node is a **trigger** (e.g. `core.trigger.manual`, id `start`), each field you bind must be declared in `variables.globals[]` as a trigger-associated input — `direction: "in"`, `triggerNodeId: "<triggerId>"` — and is then read as `$vars.<triggerId>.output.<id>`:
48	>
49	> ```json
50	> { "id": "invoiceNumber", "direction": "in", "type": "string", "triggerNodeId": "start" }
51	> ```
52	>
53	> Bind it on the agent node (`agentInputVariables[]`, `=$vars.start.output.invoiceNumber`) and reference it in the prompt as `{{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}`. Likewise, flow outputs the agent feeds (e.g. `determination`, `rationale`) must be declared as `direction: "out"` globals and mapped on every reachable End node. Full schema and the `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` access rule: [../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) (§ Input associated with a trigger); declaring/mapping mechanics: [../../editing-operations-json.md § Add a workflow variable](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-a-workflow-variable).
54	
55	| Where | What | Example |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| Flow node `inputs.agentInputVariables[]` | One entry per input — the delivery binding the converter turns into `JobArguments`. | `{ "id": "start__output__invoiceNumber", "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.start.output.invoiceNumber", "description": "Bound from $vars.start.output.invoiceNumber" }` |
58	| `agent.json` `inputSchema.properties` | One `<trigger>__output__<var>` key per input — **mandatory**, binds `JobArguments` → the agent's `input`. | `"start__output__invoiceNumber": { "type": "string", "description": "Bound from $vars.start.output.invoiceNumber" }` |
59	| `agent.json` `messages[].content` | `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` (the `input.` form — never `$vars`). | `"Invoice: {{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}"` |
60	| `agent.json` `messages[].contentTokens[]` | One `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": "input.<trigger>__output__<var>" }` per `{{ ... }}` token in `content` (brace-free `rawString`). | `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": "input.start__output__invoiceNumber" }` |
61	
62	Each binding's source `$vars.<node>.output.<field>` must reference a real node `id` in the `.flow` file, with an edge path reaching the inline-agent node. See [../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md](../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the full expression contract.
63	
64	### The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant
65	
66	`content` is the source of truth. **`uip agent refresh` regenerates `messages[].contentTokens` from `content`** (correct `simpleText`/`variable` types, brace-free `rawString`). So: author the prompt in `content`, run `refresh`, and **don't hand-author or hand-fix `contentTokens`**. `uip agent validate` is read-only — if it flags a token mismatch (`Expected type "simpleText"…`, `Expected "input.X" but got "{{input.X}}"`, or `contentTokens has N entries but content requires M`), **re-run `refresh`** to regenerate; don't edit `rawString`.
67	
68	What `refresh` produces, for `content` = `"Invoice Number: {{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}\n"`:
69	
70	```json
71	"contentTokens": [
72	  { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Invoice Number: " },
73	  { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.start__output__invoiceNumber" },
74	  { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "\n" }
75	]
76	```
77	
78	### Worked example — end to end (repeat the triple per input)
79	
80	Flow node (excerpt) — `binding` per input, typed `agentOutputVariables`:
81	
82	```json
83	"agentInputVariables": [
84	  { "id": "emailReceived1__output__subject", "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.emailReceived1.output.subject" },
85	  { "id": "emailReceived1__output__body",    "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.emailReceived1.output.body" }
86	],
87	"agentOutputVariables": [{ "id": "category", "type": "string" }]
88	```
89	
90	Matching `agent.json` — `inputSchema` keys mirror the bindings; the prompt uses the `input.` form, and `contentTokens` decompose `content` left-to-right (literals → `simpleText` verbatim incl. `\n`; each `{{ … }}` → brace-free `variable`):
91	
92	```json
93	"inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": {
94	  "emailReceived1__output__subject": { "type": "string" },
95	  "emailReceived1__output__body":    { "type": "string" }
96	} },
97	"outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "category": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["category"] },
98	"messages": [
99	  { "role": "system", "content": "Triage the email.", "contentTokens": [{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Triage the email." }] },
100	  { "role": "user",
101	    "content": "Subject: {{input.emailReceived1__output__subject}}\n\n{{input.emailReceived1__output__body}}",
102	    "contentTokens": [
103	      { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Subject: " },
104	      { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.emailReceived1__output__subject" },
105	      { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "\n\n" },
106	      { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.emailReceived1__output__body" }
107	    ] }
108	]
109	```
110	
111	Keep the flow-node `systemPrompt` / `userPrompt` as short generic placeholders — the canonical prompt lives in `agent.json messages[]`, and that system prompt should be a real structured one (see `agent-prompting-guide.md`), not a bare blob.
112	
113	### When the source field name is unknown at authoring time
114	
115	Connector-trigger output fields (e.g. email `subject`/`from`/`body`) aren't in the registry — only knowable after a real run. Author best-guess `{{input.<node>__output__<field>}}` paths with the matching `binding`/`inputSchema` key, **ask the user to confirm before upload** (don't invent field names silently), and correct the tokens + `contentTokens` mirrors after the first run.
116	
117	### Anti-patterns
118	
119	- **In `agent.json` prompts, use the `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` form** (the flattened key, `input.` prefix). Never use raw `{{ $vars.X }}` (the runtime can't resolve it — agent gets the literal token) or `{{plainName}}` (no prefix).
120	- **The `variable` `rawString` is exactly what sits between the braces** — `input.<trigger>__output__<var>`, brace-free, no added spaces.
121	- **Keep the flow-node `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` as short generic placeholders** — the canonical prompt lives in `agent.json messages[]`, and delivery comes from `agentInputVariables[]`, not from tokens in the node prompts.
122	- **Each `agentInputVariables[]` entry uses `binding` (not `value`).** The converter builds `JobArguments` from `binding`; a `value: "=js:$vars…"` entry (Studio Web's internal canvas form) is **ignored** — the agent gets empty input and faults at debug (`AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR`, "Template placeholders detected instead of actual values"). Write `{ "id": "<key>", "binding": "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. `binding` is what both the CLI converter and Studio Web's loader read.
123

141	## Adding / Editing
142	
143	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Inline-agent scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but the flow graph is not a Flow CLI carve-out: add the `uipath.agent.autonomous` node, its `inputs.source`, outputs, variables, layout, and edges directly in the `.flow` JSON with `Edit` / `Write`.
144	
145	### Add the node with Edit / Write
146	
147	Use `Edit` to add a node instance to `nodes[]`. The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`. Do not write a node instance `model` block for `uipath.agent.autonomous`: flow-core's `createNodeFromManifest` hoists manifest-declared `source` identity into `inputs.source` and returns a node with no `model`.

150	{
151	  "id": "autonomousAgent1",
152	  "type": "uipath.agent.autonomous",
153	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
154	  "display": { "label": "Autonomous Agent" },
155	  "inputs": {
156	    "systemPrompt": "You are an agentic assistant.",
157	    "userPrompt": "What is the current date?",
158	    "source": "<projectId-uuid>",
159	    "agentInputVariables": [],
160	    "agentOutputVariables": [
161	      { "id": "content", "type": "string" }
162	    ]
163	  },
164	  "outputs": {
165	    "output": {
166	      "type": "object",
167	      "description": "Agent response",
168	      "source": "=result.response",
169	      "var": "output"
170	    },
171	    "error": {
172	      "type": "object",
173	      "description": "Error information if the node fails",
174	      "source": "=Error",
175	      "var": "error"
176	    }
177	  }
178	}
179	```

182	
183	- A `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get uipath.agent.autonomous --output json` (`Data.Node` or the top-level node object, depending on CLI/plugin version). Set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
184	- `variables.nodes[]` entries for `autonomousAgent1.output` and `autonomousAgent1.error` with `binding.nodeId = "autonomousAgent1"` and matching `binding.outputId` values.

188	
189	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`:
190	
191	```json
192	{
193	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
194	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
195	  "sourcePort": "output",
196	  "targetNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
197	  "targetPort": "input"
198	}
199	```

202	{
203	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
204	  "sourceNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
205	  "sourcePort": "success",
206	  "targetNodeId": "<nextNodeId>",
207	  "targetPort": "input"
208	}

214	{
215	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
216	  "sourceNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
217	  "sourcePort": "tool",
218	  "targetNodeId": "<toolNodeId>",
219	  "targetPort": "input"
220	}

225	## Adding Resource Nodes
226	
227	An inline agent attaches resource nodes — tools (external or built-in), contexts, and escalations — to its three artifact ports. **All kinds wire into the `.flow` identically:** discover the node type, add a minimal node instance, copy its definition into `definitions[]`, add a placeholder layout entry, wire ONE artifact edge to the node's `input` port, then hand-author `resource.json` and run refresh + validate. Three things vary per kind — the **artifact port** the edge leaves, the **node type**, and whether the resource needs **solution-level files**. The `resource.json` body is owned by the `uipath-agents` skill (linked per row).
228	
229	| Kind | Edge source port | Node type | `resource.json` discriminator | Needs `uip solution resources refresh`? | `resource.json` reference (uipath-agents) |
230	|------|------------------|-----------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
231	| RPA process tool | `tool` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.process.<release-key>` | `type: "process"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` |
232	| Agent tool | `tool` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent.<release-key>` | `type: "agent"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` |
233	| API workflow tool | `tool` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.api.<release-key>` | `type: "api"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` |
234	| Process Orchestration tool | `tool` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.processorchestration.<release-key>` | `type: "processOrchestration"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` |
235	| Built-in tool | `tool` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.builtin.<toolType>` | `type: "internal"` | **No** — self-contained at the agent level | `lowcode/capabilities/built-in-tools/built-in-tools.md` |
236	| Context (index / RAG) | `context` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.context.index.<index-name>.<index-id>` | `$resourceType: "context"`, `contextType: "index"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/context/index.md` |
237	| Escalation (HITL) | `escalation` (top) | `uipath.agent.resource.escalation` | `$resourceType: "escalation"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/escalation/escalation.md` |
238	
239	### 1. Discover the node type and generate a UUID
240	
241	The four process-tool kinds and context carry a per-resource suffix (`<release-key>` or `<index-name>.<index-id>`) — `registry search` by the prefix (the node type minus the suffix), then `registry get` the matching `NodeType`. Escalation and built-in tools are exact strings — `registry get` directly.
242	
243	```bash
244	# Suffix-bearing kinds (process/agent/api/processorchestration tools, context):
245	uip maestro flow registry search "<prefix>" --output json   # e.g. "uipath.agent.resource.tool.process"
246	uip maestro flow registry get "<NodeType>" --output json
247	
248	# Exact-string kinds:
249	uip maestro flow registry get uipath.agent.resource.escalation --output json
250	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.agent.resource.tool.builtin.<toolType>" --output json
251	
252	# One resource UUID — used as both inputs.source and the resource.json directory/id
253	RES=$(uuidgen)
254	```
255	
256	`<release-key>` is the resource's release-key GUID from `uip solution resources list` (the row's `Key`). `<toolType>` is the built-in's fixed kebab discriminator (e.g. `analyze-attachments`), identical to the `resource.json` `properties.toolType`.
257	
258	### 2. Add the node and wire the artifact edge
259	
260	Every resource node uses the same minimal instance — `inputs.source` only, no instance `model` block. The definition declares `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity field onto `inputs.source` (same hoisting rule as `uipath.agent.autonomous`).
261	
262	```json
263	{
264	  "id": "agentTool1",
265	  "type": "<NodeType>",
266	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
267	  "display": { "label": "<Label>" },
268	  "inputs": { "source": "<RES_UUID>" }
269	}
270	```
271	
272	Also add:
273	
274	- The node definition copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`. Set `typeVersion` to its `version`.
275	- Top-level `bindings[]` entries when the definition declares `model.bindings` — process tools use `model.bindings.resourceKey` and `model.bindings.values[]` (`name`, `folderPath`, etc.); see [editing-operations-json.md — Resource nodes](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-a-node). Built-in tools declare none.
276	- A placeholder `layout.nodes.<nodeId>` entry.
277	- ONE artifact edge from the agent's port (per the matrix) to the node's `input` port. Substitute `tool` / `context` / `escalation` for `sourcePort`:
278	
279	```json
280	{
281	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
282	  "sourceNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
283	  "sourcePort": "tool",
284	  "targetNodeId": "agentTool1",
285	  "targetPort": "input"
286	}
287	```
288	
289	### 3. Author `resource.json`
290	
291	Hand-author `<FlowProjectDir>/<inlineAgentProjectId>/resources/<RES_UUID>/resource.json` using the matrix reference for the kind. Set `id` to `<RES_UUID>` (= the node's `inputs.source` and the resource directory name). A `resource.json` missing its `$resourceType` (or `type` for built-ins) is not recognized by `uip agent validate` — it reports `"resources": 0`, and the next refresh writes an empty `bindings_v2.json`.
292	
293	**Process / agent / api / processOrchestration tools** share one shape — use the exact shape in the `uipath-agents` skill: `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` § Tool resource.json Shape (read it first). The subtype is the `type` field (§ Subtypes in `process.md`). RPA uses raw .NET arrays (Template A in `solution-files.md`); Agent / API / Process Orchestration use JSON Schema V2 (Template B). Run `uip solution resources list` + `uip solution resources get` to populate `referenceKey`, `folderPath`, `inputSchema`, `outputSchema`. Inline-in-flow specifics:
294	
295	- Set `location` from the discovery `Source` field: `"solution"` when `Source: "Local"`, `"external"` when `Source: "Remote"` (same rule as standalone agents).
296	- Set `properties.folderPath` to the **literal folder path from discovery** (e.g., `"Shared/TestRPA"`) — do **not** leave it empty.
297	- `inputSchema.properties` must include `"guardrails": { "type": "array" }` alongside the process arguments.
298	
299	**Built-in, context, and escalation** bodies follow their matrix reference.
300	
301	### 4. Refresh, validate, refresh solution resources
302	
303	Set prompts in `agent.json` (system + user `messages` with `contentTokens` of `type: "simpleText"` and `rawString`), then:
304	
305	```bash
306	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow \
307	  --bindings-target "<FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json" --output json
308	uip agent validate "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
309	# All kinds EXCEPT built-in tools:
310	uip solution resources refresh --output json
311	```
312	
313	- **Process tools / context / escalation** resolve through `bindings_v2.json` (process / index / App binding). Pass `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` on refresh so `uip solution resources refresh` discovers the binding and writes the solution-level files. Do not hand-edit `bindings_v2.json` — refresh regenerates it.
314	- **Built-in tools** carry `referenceKey: null` and `type: "internal"` — no `bindings[]`, no solution-level files, no `uip solution resources refresh`.
315	- **Verify both refresh and validate report `"resources": N` where N > 0.** If either shows `"resources": 0`, the `resource.json` is malformed or missing required fields — fix it and re-run before proceeding.
316	
317	For agent.json prompt configuration and solution resource mechanics, see the `uipath-agents` skill (`lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md`).

319	## JSON Structure
320	
321	The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
322	
323	```json
324	{
325	  "id": "autonomousAgent1",
326	  "type": "uipath.agent.autonomous",
327	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
328	  "display": { "label": "Autonomous Agent" },
329	  "inputs": {
330	    "systemPrompt": "You are an agentic assistant.",
331	    "userPrompt": "What is the current date?",
332	    "source": "<projectId-uuid>",
333	    "agentInputVariables": [],
334	    "agentOutputVariables": [
335	      { "id": "content", "type": "string" }
336	    ]
337	  },
338	  "outputs": {
339	    "output": {
340	      "type": "object",
341	      "description": "Agent response",
342	      "source": "=result.response",
343	      "var": "output"
344	    },
345	    "error": {
346	      "type": "object",
347	      "description": "Error information if the node fails",
348	      "source": "=Error",
349	      "var": "error"
350	    }
351	  }
352	}
353	```
354	
355	Notes:
356	
357	- `inputs.source` — the inline agent's `projectId`; must match the subdirectory name and `agent.json.projectId`. The definition still declares `model.source: true`, but flow-core hoists that identity field onto `inputs.source` for the node instance.
358	- `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` must be non-empty for current `flow validate`. Treat them as validator placeholders; the canonical inline-agent prompts live in `agent.json`.
359	- `inputs.agentInputVariables` carries one entry per flow input the agent reads — `{ id: "<trigger>__output__<var>", binding: "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. This is the only thing the converter turns into the runtime `JobArguments`; prompts then reference each input as `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` (see § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts above). Leave it `[]` only when the agent reads no flow data.
360	- **No `model` block on the inline-agent node instance.** The node inherits serviceType/version/context from `definitions[]`; `source` lives at `inputs.source`. Stale instance fields such as `model.serviceType`, `model.version`, or `model.context` override the inherited definition and can cause runtime mismatch.
361	
362	## Accessing Output
363	
364	How agent output surfaces depends on `agent.json` `outputSchema`:
365	
366	- **Typed `outputSchema`** (the required form — step 5) — each property surfaces **flat** at `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>`. For `outputSchema.properties` `{ subject, body }`: read `$vars.<nodeId>.output.subject` and `$vars.<nodeId>.output.body`. **There is no `.content.` wrapper** — `$vars.<nodeId>.output.content.subject` resolves to undefined and silently yields a null flow output.
367	- **Untyped (single string)** — only when no typed schema is declared: `$vars.<nodeId>.output.content` holds the agent's text response.
368	- `$vars.<nodeId>.error` — error details if the agent fails.
369	
370	To expose a typed field as a flow output, see § Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs below.
371	
372	## Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs
373	
374	Symmetric to input wiring — **three aligned pieces**, none CLI-derived:
375	
376	| Where | What | Example |
377	| --- | --- | --- |
378	| `agent.json` `outputSchema.properties` | One typed key per field the agent returns. | `"subject": { "type": "string" }`, `"body": { "type": "string" }` |
379	| Flow node `inputs.agentOutputVariables[]` | **One entry per field** — NOT a single `content` object. | `[{ "id": "subject", "type": "string" }, { "id": "body", "type": "string" }]` |
380	| End node `outputs.<global>` | Maps each `out` global to the flat field path. | `"emailBody": { "source": "=js:$vars.<agentNodeId>.output.body" }` |
381	
382	Plus: declare each flow output as a `direction: "out"` global in `variables.globals[]`, and map it on **every reachable End node**.
383	
384	**Anti-pattern:** `agentOutputVariables: [{ "id": "content", "type": "object" }]` paired with End `=js:$vars.<node>.output.content.<field>`. The typed agent delivers fields flat at `output.<field>`; the `.content.` path resolves to undefined → `flow validate` passes, debug Completes, but the flow output is **null**.
385	
386	## Refresh and Validate
387	
388	Refresh the inline agent (writes `entry-points.json` and `bindings_v2.json`, and for tool-bearing agents, propagates bindings into the flow project's `bindings_v2.json`), then validate (read-only check), then validate the flow:
389	
390	```bash
391	# 1. Refresh the inline agent (writes entry-points.json and bindings_v2.json)
392	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
393	
394	# 1b. For tool-bearing inline agents, refresh with --bindings-target to propagate tool bindings:
395	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow \
396	  --bindings-target "<FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json" --output json
397	
398	# 2. Validate the inline agent (read-only schema check)
399	uip agent validate "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
400	
401	# 3. Validate the flow
402	uip maestro flow validate <FlowName>.flow --output json
403	```
404	
405	> Current validator requirement: `uip maestro flow validate` rejects flows whose `uipath.agent.autonomous` node lacks non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt`. Include placeholder values on the flow node, but keep the canonical prompts in the inline agent's `agent.json`.
406	
407	## Debug
408	
409	| Error | Cause | Fix |
410	| --- | --- | --- |
411	| `flow validate` reports `systemPrompt` / `userPrompt` required | The flow node lacks non-empty validator placeholders, the `inputs.source` UUID is missing, or the inline agent subdirectory cannot be found | Add non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` placeholders, set `inputs.source` to the inline agent UUID, and verify `<FlowDir>/<projectId>/agent.json` exists |
412	| `inputs.source` UUID does not match any subdirectory | Wrong source value, or folder renamed | Set `inputs.source` to the exact UUID of the inline agent directory |
413	| Flow runs a different agent than expected | `inputs.source` points to a stale/leftover inline agent dir | Check subdirectory names — only one inline agent dir should correspond to each agent node |
414	| `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob` error at runtime | Stale instance `model` fields override the inherited inline-agent definition | Remove the inline-agent node's instance `model` block and keep the registry definition's `model.serviceType: "Orchestrator.StartInlineAgentJob"` in `definitions[]` |
415	| Studio Web reports "System prompt is required" | Inline agent's `agent.json.messages[]` has empty `content`, OR derived files (`entry-points.json`, `bindings_v2.json`) are stale | Set prompts in `agent.json`, re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` to regenerate derived files, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check — see `uipath-agents` skill |
416	| Studio Web debug: "Could not find process for tool" | Flow project's `bindings_v2.json` is missing the tool's process binding, so `uip solution resources refresh` never created the solution-level resource | Re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` to propagate bindings, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check schema, then `uip solution resources refresh`, then re-upload |
417	| `bindings_v2.json` is empty or missing tool bindings | Tool bindings were not propagated to the flow project level, or a later tool overwrote the file | Re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` after all flow node and edge edits are complete. Refresh is the verb that writes the file — do not hand-edit it |
418	| Agent tool (process / agent / api / processOrchestration) cannot resolve at runtime | Missing top-level `bindings[]` entries, mismatched tool-node `inputs.source` / `resource.json` id, stale solution resources, or missing project-level `bindings_v2.json` | Add the resource bindings from the tool definition, keep the tool node's `inputs.source` equal to the resource UUID, run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` to write bindings, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check, then run `uip solution resources refresh` |
419	| `inputs.agentProjectId` unrecognized | Wrong field name | Use `inputs.source` — `agentProjectId` is not valid for inline agents |
420	| Inline agent rejected by `uip agent validate` | `entry-points.json` or `project.uiproj` present inside the inline agent dir | Delete those files — they belong only to standalone agent projects |
421	| Folder name is human-readable instead of UUID | Folder renamed after scaffolding | Rename to the original `projectId` UUID — the folder name must match `inputs.source` and the `projectId` field inside `agent.json` |
422	| Agent runs but returns empty `output.content` | Missing or malformed `contentTokens` in `agent.json` | Rebuild `messages[].contentTokens` using `{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "..." }` entries; see `uipath-agents` for detail |
423	| `flow validate` passes, debug Completes, but the `out` global (e.g. `emailBody`) is null | Typed agent output read with a `.content.` wrapper — `agentOutputVariables:[{content}]` + End `=js:$vars.<node>.output.content.<field>` — but typed fields surface flat at `output.<field>` | List each field in `agentOutputVariables[]` (`{id:"subject"},{id:"body"}`) and map End to `=js:$vars.<node>.output.<field>` (no `.content.`). See § Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs. |
424	| `agent validate` flags `Expected type "simpleText" but got "text"` | Hand-edited `contentToken` written with `type: "text"` | Re-run `uip agent refresh` — it regenerates `contentTokens` from `content` (correct `simpleText`/`variable` types). Don't hand-edit the token. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
425	| `agent validate` flags `Expected "input.X" but got "{{input.X}}"` | Hand-edited `variable` token has the braces/extra spaces in its `rawString` | Re-run `uip agent refresh` to regenerate the tokens from `content` (brace-free `rawString`) — don't hand-fix it. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
426	| `agent validate` flags `contentTokens has N entries but content requires M. Rebuild contentTokens to match content.` | `content` and `contentTokens` drifted (e.g. tokens edited without `content`, or vice versa) | Re-run `uip agent refresh` to regenerate `contentTokens` from `content`. If the prompt itself is wrong, fix `content` first, then refresh. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
427	| Prompt shows literal `{{input.X}}` at runtime | `inputSchema.properties` missing the referenced key (`flow validate` flags this — run it) | Add the `<trigger>__output__<var>` key to `inputSchema`. |
428	| `flow validate` passes but debug faults `AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR` (literal `input.<key>`) | Node `agentInputVariables` uses `value:` instead of `binding:` (or is missing) → empty `JobArguments` | Set `binding:"=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>"` on the node entry; ensure the trigger global is declared (`direction:"in"`). |
429	| Debug faults `AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR` "Template placeholders detected instead of actual values" — and the node *does* have `agentInputVariables[]` | Entries use `value: "=js:$vars…"` (Studio Web's canvas form) instead of `binding`; the converter only reads `binding`, so `JobArguments` are empty | Rename `value` → `binding` on each entry and strip the `=js:` prefix: `{ "id": "<key>", "binding": "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. See § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts. |
430	
431	## Repair Recipes
432	
433	Use direct JSON edits for inline-agent graph repairs. The Flow CLI has no node-update command (see [editing-operations-cli.md § Operations Not Supported by CLI](../../editing-operations-cli.md#operations-not-supported-by-cli)), and the inline-agent graph is not a Flow CLI carve-out. If a bulk scripted rewrite is explicitly approved, use the `python3` heredoc pattern from [editing-operations-json.md — Edit Tooling](../../editing-operations-json.md#edit-tooling); otherwise apply the same transformations through `Edit` / `Write`.
434	
435	### Replace a definition entry
436	
437	Use when the `definitions[]` entry for a node type is wrong, stale, or hand-written. The fix is always: re-fetch from the registry, splice into `definitions[]` matching on `nodeType`, then keep the node instance minimal.
438	
439	```bash
440	uip maestro flow registry get uipath.agent.autonomous --output json > /tmp/registry_response.json
441	python3 - <<'PY'
442	import json
443	new_def = json.load(open("/tmp/registry_response.json"))["Data"]["Node"]
444	flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
445	for i, d in enumerate(flow["definitions"]):
446	    if d.get("nodeType") == "uipath.agent.autonomous":
447	        flow["definitions"][i] = new_def
448	        break
449	INLINE_TYPES = ("uipath.agent.autonomous", "uipath.agent.resource.")
450	for node in flow["nodes"]:
451	    t = node.get("type", "")
452	    if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
453	        model = node.pop("model", None) or {}
454	        if isinstance(model.get("source"), str):
455	            node.setdefault("inputs", {})["source"] = model["source"]
456	json.dump(flow, open("<FILE>.flow", "w"), indent=2)
457	PY
458	uip maestro flow validate <FILE>.flow --output json
459	```
460	
461	Same pattern works for any node type — substitute the `nodeType` string in both the `registry get` command and the loop guard. The `model.source` → `inputs.source` rewrite above is applied to both the inline agent node and every attached resource node (tool, escalation, context) — all of them carry source identity at `inputs.source` and never on an instance `model` block.
462	
463	### Resolve a `[REQUIRED_FIELD] systemPrompt is required` validator error
464	
465	Current flow validation requires non-empty placeholder prompts on the flow node and uses the inline agent directory referenced by `inputs.source`. Check in order:
466	
467	1. **UUID at `inputs.source`** — the `projectId` UUID must be set at `inputs.source`. Diagnose:
468	
469	    ```bash
470	    python3 - <<'PY'
471	    import json
472	    flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
473	    for node in flow["nodes"]:
474	        t = node.get("type", "")
475	        if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
476	            print(t, "inputs.source:", node.get("inputs", {}).get("source"))
477	            print(t, "model.source: ", node.get("model", {}).get("source"))
478	    PY
479	    ```
480	
481	    If a stale flow has the UUID at `model.source` on the inline agent node **or any attached resource node** (tool, escalation, context), move it to `inputs.source` and remove the instance `model` block:
482	
483	    ```bash
484	    python3 - <<'PY'
485	    import json
486	    flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
487	    for node in flow["nodes"]:
488	        t = node.get("type", "")
489	        if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
490	            inputs = node.setdefault("inputs", {})
491	            model = node.pop("model", None) or {}
492	            uuid = model.get("source")
493	            if uuid:
494	                inputs["source"] = uuid
495	    json.dump(flow, open("<FILE>.flow", "w"), indent=2)
496	    PY
497	    ```
498	
499	2. **Subdirectory** — confirm `<FlowDir>/<projectId>/` exists and contains `agent.json`. If not, re-run `uip agent init "<FlowDir>" --inline-in-flow --output json` and bind the returned `ProjectId` through `inputs.source`.
500	
501	3. **Prompts in `agent.json`** — set `messages[0].content` (system) and `messages[1].content` (user) to real prompts before validate. Rebuild `messages[].contentTokens` to match — `[{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "<your prompt text>" }]` per message.
502	
503	4. **Validator placeholders on the flow node** — add non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` and `inputs.userPrompt` placeholders if they are missing. These are for current `flow validate`; keep the canonical prompt text in `agent.json`.
504	
505	## What NOT to Do
506	
507	- **Do not use Flow CLI `node add`, `edge add`, or `variable` commands for inline-agent graph edits** — inline-agent node, edge, variable, layout, and tool-resource node changes are non-carve-out structural `.flow` mutations and must be authored directly with `Edit` / `Write`.
508	- **Do not treat `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` as canonical prompts** — current validation requires non-empty placeholders on the flow node, but prompts live in `agent.json`.
509	- **Do not put a `model` block on the inline-agent node instance** — the node inherits serviceType/version/context from `definitions[]`; the inline-agent source lives at `inputs.source`.
510	- **Do not use `model.agentProjectId`, `inputs.agentProjectId`, or `model.source` on any inline-agent-related node instance** — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached resource node (`uipath.agent.resource.tool.*`, `uipath.agent.resource.escalation`, `uipath.agent.resource.context.*`) carry source identity at `inputs.source` and have no instance `model` block.
511	- **Do not create `entry-points.json` or `project.uiproj` inside the inline agent directory** — those belong only to standalone agent projects.
512	- **Do not name the inline agent folder with a human-readable name** — the folder name must be the `projectId` UUID.
513	- **Do not use `uip agent tool add`** for inline-in-flow agents — hand-author the tool's `resource.json` instead.
514	- **Do not skip `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` followed by `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow`** after editing `agent.json` or any `resources/*/resource.json`; for tool-bearing inline agents, pass `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` on the refresh call to propagate tool bindings.
515

1	# API Workflow Node — Implementation
2	
3	API workflow nodes invoke API functions. Pattern: `uipath.core.api-workflow.{key}`.
4	
5	## Discovery
6	
7	### Published (tenant registry)
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
11	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.api-workflow" --output json
12	```
13	
14	### In-solution (sibling projects)
15	
16	```bash
17	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
18	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
19	```
20	
21	## Registry Validation
22	
23	```bash
24	# Published
25	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.api-workflow.{key}" --output json
26	
27	# In-solution
28	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.api-workflow.{key}" --local --output json
29	```
30	
31	Confirm:
32	
33	- Input port: `input`
34	- Output port: `output`
35	- `model.serviceType` — `Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflowAsync`
36	- `model.bindings.resourceSubType` — `Api`
37	- `model.bindings.resourceKey` — the `<FolderPath>.<ApiName>` string used to scope binding resolution
38	- `inputDefinition` — typically empty
39	- `outputDefinition.error` — error schema
40	
41	## Adding / Editing
42	
43	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure below for the node-specific `inputs`.
44	
45	## JSON Structure
46	
47	### Node instance (inside `nodes[]`)
48	
49	The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and binding/context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "id": "callApiFunction",
54	  "type": "uipath.core.api-workflow.346b8959-c126-48d3-9c46-942abcf944d7",
55	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
56	  "display": { "label": "Call API Function" },
57	  "inputs": {},
58	  "outputs": {
59	    "output": {
60	      "type": "object",
61	      "description": "The return value of the API workflow",
62	      "source": "=result.response",
63	      "var": "output"
64	    },
65	    "error": {
66	      "type": "object",
67	      "description": "Error information if the API workflow fails",
68	      "source": "=result.Error",
69	      "var": "error"
70	    }
71	  }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	### Top-level `bindings[]` entries (sibling of `nodes`/`edges`/`definitions`)
76	
77	Add one entry per `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)` pair. Share entries across node instances that reference the same API workflow — do NOT create duplicates.
78	
79	```json
80	"bindings": [
81	  {
82	    "id": "bCallApiFunctionName",
83	    "name": "name",
84	    "type": "string",
85	    "resource": "process",
86	    "resourceKey": "Shared.My API Function",
87	    "default": "My API Function",
88	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
89	    "resourceSubType": "Api"
90	  },
91	  {
92	    "id": "bCallApiFunctionFolderPath",
93	    "name": "folderPath",
94	    "type": "string",
95	    "resource": "process",
96	    "resourceKey": "Shared.My API Function",
97	    "default": "Shared",
98	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
99	    "resourceSubType": "Api"
100	  }
101	]
102	```
103	
104	> For the resolution mechanics and why these entries are required, see [file-format.md — Bindings](../../../../shared/file-format.md#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings).
105	
106	## Debug
107	
108	| Error | Cause | Fix |
109	| --- | --- | --- |
110	| Node type not found in registry | API workflow not published or registry stale | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`; for in-solution API workflows use `--local` |
111	| Execution failed | Underlying API workflow errored | Check `$vars.{nodeId}.error` for details |
112

7	## Registry Validation

33	        "expression": "$vars.classify.output.priority === 'medium'"
34	      },
35	      {
36	        "id": "low",
37	        "label": "Low Priority",
38	        "expression": "$vars.classify.output.priority === 'low'"
39	      }
40	    ]

45	## Adding / Editing
46	
47	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs`.

49	## Wiring
50	
51	Each case creates a dynamic output port `case-{id}`. An optional `default` port handles unmatched values. Ensure edge `sourcePort` matches `case-{id}` exactly. See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.

54	
55	| Error | Cause | Fix |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| No case matched, no default wired | All case expressions false and no default edge | Add a `default` edge or ensure cases are exhaustive |
58	| Case expression error | Invalid JavaScript in case expression | Check `=js:` expression syntax |

1	# End Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.control.end`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, no output ports. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Without Output Mapping
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "doneSuccess",
22	  "type": "core.control.end",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
25	  "inputs": {}
26	}
27	```
28	
29	### With Output Mapping
30	
31	When the workflow declares `out` variables, every End node must map all of them:
32	
33	```json
34	{
35	  "id": "doneSuccess",
36	  "type": "core.control.end",
37	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
38	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
39	  "inputs": {},
40	  "outputs": {
41	    "processedCount": {
42	      "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output.count"
43	    },
44	    "resultSummary": {
45	      "source": "=js:$vars.formatOutput.output.summary"
46	    }
47	  }
48	}
49	```
50	
51	Each key in `outputs` must match a variable `id` from `variables.globals` where `direction: "out"`.
52	
53	## Adding / Editing
54	
55	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `outputs`.
56	
57	Output mapping must be added with `Edit` against the `.flow` file — see [Edit/Write: Add output mapping](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-output-mapping-on-an-end-node).
58	
59	## Debug
60	
61	| Error | Cause | Fix |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| Missing output mapping | `out` variable not mapped on this End node | Add `outputs.{varId}.source` expression for every `out` variable |
64	| Output expression unresolvable | `$vars` reference points to unreachable node | Ensure the node is upstream and connected via edges |
65	| Runtime silent failure | Output mapping missing on one reachable End node | Check **all** End nodes, not just the primary path |

1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 615 616 ```json 617 { 618 "variables": { 619 "globals": [ 620 { 621 "id": "inputItems", 622 "direction": "in", 623 "type": "array", 624 "subType": "object", 625 "defaultValue": [], 626 "description": "Items to process" 627 }, 628 { 629 "id": "processedCount", 630 "direction": "inout", 631 "type": "number", 632 "defaultValue": 0 633 }, 634 { 635 "id": "result", 636 "direction": "out", 637 "type": "object", 638 "description": "Processing summary" 639 } 640 ], 641 "nodes": [ 642 { 643 "id": "transform1.output", 644 "type": "object", 645 "binding": { "nodeId": "transform1", "outputId": "output" } 646 } 647 ], 648 "variableUpdates": { 649 "transform1": [ 650 { 651 "variableId": "processedCount", 652 "expression": "=js:$vars.processedCount + $vars.transform1.output.count" 653 } 654 ] 655 } 656 }, 657 "nodes": [ 658 { 659 "id": "start", 660 "type": "core.trigger.manual", 661 "typeVersion": "1.0", 662 "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" }, 663 "inputs": { 664 "entryPointId": "" 665 }, 666 "outputs": { 667 "output": { 668 "type": "object", 669 "description": "The return value of the trigger.", 670 "source": "=result.response", 671 "var": "output" 672 } 673 } 674 }, 675 { 676 "id": "transform1", 677 "type": "core.action.script", 678 "typeVersion": "1.0", 679 "inputs": { 680 "script": "const items = $vars.inputItems.filter(i => i.active);\nreturn { count:
